voice.name: Test Voice
voice.direction: curious, conversational, slightly amused; clear contrast between question ([curious]), discovery ([warmly]) and limitation ([softly] / [dryly]); never a promotional announcer

timing.lead_in_note: silent hide before s02 (v1 s01 is cut; the hide is picture only)
timing.pause_rule: pause_ms is the gap to the next line, applied as a cap: trim a take's own longer paragraph pause to it (v1 overshot 16 gaps)

estimate.method: v1 takes at their measured spans (minus the listed in-line pause tightening); new lines that repeat a v1 sentence at that fragment's measured length; other new lines at 170 wpm (questions 160); plus every pause_ms, the 1.0 s lead-in and a 10.0 s end screen

lines.text: That sensor can't see him. It's pointed at a plain, blank wall.
lines.tts: That sensor can't see him. It's pointed at a plain, blank wall.
lines.direction: VOICE: matter-of-fact setup (v1 take); if the new hook takes (block y01) sound unlike it, regenerate it with y01, same words, under a new id. PICTURE: 1.0 s silent hide first (he tiptoes in, settles smug); sensor-facing room view: the dashed sight line from the sensor stops at the partition with an X on 'can't see him'; then the S1.2 push: the checker taps the sensor, its field-of-view wedge lights bare wall well clear of him; labels 'sensor' 'blocked'.

lines.text: Yet researchers have used light bouncing off a wall to track someone hidden around a corner.
lines.tts: Yet… researchers have used light bouncing off a wall to track someone hidden around a corner.
lines.direction: VOICE: a small beat after 'Yet', then clear and quietly amazed: the discovery, not an announcement. PICTURE: hard cut on 'researchers' to the full-frame real board (kraft, 'Real data'): authors' stored estimate from index 6, every 2nd frame, sped up; labels 'sensor' 'blocked' 'estimated position'; one source line.

lines.text: That dot is their position estimate. Not a photograph.
lines.tts: That dot is their position estimate. [dryly] Not a photograph.
lines.direction: VOICE: plain, then a dry drop on 'Not a photograph' (said once in the film). PICTURE: same board, 5% push to the dot; 0.6 s hold for reading; cut-in of the guesser's smirk freezing (our room, never synced to the track).

lines.text: The trick is timing: light that reaches him takes the long way round, so it comes back later.
lines.tts: [warmly] The trick is timing: light that reaches him takes the long way round… so it comes back later.
lines.direction: VOICE: friendly explainer; light stress on 'long way round'. PICTURE: match cut to our full-frame plan schematic (chip 'illustration'): short teal trip S to W1 and back races the long saffron trip S to W1 to him to W1 to S, around the partition's end; both drop onto one timeline.

lines.text: A few billionths of a second later.
lines.tts: [dryly] A few billionths of a second later.
lines.direction: VOICE: dry undercut on the size of 'later'. PICTURE: the arrival timeline fills the frame: tall teal wall echo first, small saffron echo later, bracket 'a few nanoseconds'; 'not to scale'; no number.

v1_fragment_alt.use: only if the listening pass prefers it to the new take and it splices cleanly; cut inside the measured silence

lines.text: This takes a time-of-flight sensor, a camera that clocks its own light's round trip.
lines.tts: This takes a time-of-flight sensor… a camera that clocks its own light's round trip.
lines.direction: VOICE: define the sensor plainly. PICTURE: timeline shrinks into the sensor's display (chart to display match); sensor close-up; label 'time-of-flight sensor'; chip 'invisible flash · shown for clarity'; the checker taps the display.

v1_fragment_alt.use: only if the listening pass prefers it to the new take and it splices cleanly; cut inside the measured silence

lines.text: So how do you turn a tiny delay into a location?
lines.tts: [curious] So how do you turn a tiny delay… into a location?
lines.direction: VOICE: a real question, rising, unhurried; the hook ends here. PICTURE: push past the sensor into the plan; W1 glows; a dashed candidate arc starts from W1, stops a third of the way and resolves into a '?'; the camera pushes into W1's paint.

lines.text: First, a puzzle: why does a plain wall work at all?
lines.tts: [curious] First, a puzzle… why does a plain wall work at all?
lines.direction: VOICE: 'First' marks this as step one of the answer, not a change of subject; curious, a small beat after 'puzzle'. PICTURE: the push into W1's paint pulls back out to the raised room view: bare wall, sensor, him behind the partition; question title 'What survives the bounce?' for this line only.

lines.text: Put a mirror here, and our friend is simply visible.
lines.tts: [dryly] Put a mirror here… and our friend is simply visible.
lines.direction: VOICE: dry; J2 lands on 'visible'. PICTURE: same raised view; on 'here' the checker slides a mirror panel onto the wall; one pulse runs sensor to mirror to him with 1 s 'in = out' angle marks; the mirror shows his back; J2: he ducks; hold 0.5 s.

v1_fragment_alt.use: only if the listening pass prefers it to the new take and it splices cleanly; cut inside the measured silence

lines.text: A painted wall is rough up close. It throws light every which way, so each spot acts less like a mirror, more like a tiny lamp.
lines.tts: A painted wall is rough up close. It throws light every which way, so each spot acts less like a mirror, more like a tiny lamp.
lines.direction: VOICE: explainer (v1 take). PICTURE: the guesser slides the mirror off, relieved; magnifier irises into the paint cross-section; one ray sprays every which way; labels 'rough up close' 'tiny lamp (our analogy)'.

lines.text: Everything coming back is a blend of many paths. What survives is timing.
lines.tts: Everything coming back is a blend of many paths… [warmly] What survives is timing.
lines.direction: VOICE: the section's thesis; small lift on 'timing'. PICTURE: iris out to the room: paths from his head, shoulder and feet via three wall spots merge into one blip at the sensor; the blip lands on the hook's timeline; label 'what survives: timing'.

v1_fragment_alt.use: only if the listening pass prefers it to the new take and it splices cleanly; cut inside the measured silence

lines.text: Nearly everything coming back bounced once, off the wall. Our friend's echo bounced three times, so it's tiny.
lines.tts: Nearly everything coming back bounced once, off the wall. Our friend's echo bounced three times, so it's tiny.
lines.direction: VOICE: plain; 'tiny' small (v1 take; tighten the pause after 'wall.' from 0.54 to 0.35 s). PICTURE: the hook's timeline fills the frame with a five-icon route strip above it (sensor, wall, him, wall, sensor); one pulse thins at each bounce; tall '1 bounce' spike, then the tiny late '3 bounces' bump ringed on 'tiny'; 'not to scale · far weaker'.

lines.text: This is real data from the same team, with a different sensor and hidden object: the wall's big echo, then, a few nanoseconds later, a bump you have to zoom in to see. In this capture, hundreds of times weaker.
lines.tts: This is real data from the same team, with a different sensor and hidden object: the wall's big echo, then, a few nanoseconds later, a bump you have to zoom in to see. [softly] In this capture, hundreds of times weaker.
lines.direction: VOICE: evidence voice, careful (v1 take). PICTURE: short music drop, hard switch to the real waveform board (3x3 zone icon, 'Real data'); trace drawn from frame 1; wall echo named; magnifier stretches the tail x250 until the bump shows.

lines.text: That bump is the clue. Its timing says how much farther the light travelled.
lines.tts: That bump is the clue. Its timing says how much farther the light travelled.
lines.direction: VOICE: short, confident (v1 take; tighten the pause after 'clue.' to 0.35 s). PICTURE: bump ringed; dimension line spike to bump; labels '≈ 3.7 ns later' '≈ 1.1 m extra, there and back'; the checker's pointer taps the ring; ring cuts to a ring round W1.

lines.text: Farther from where? Simplify it: the sensor flashes and listens at one spot on the wall.
lines.tts: [curious] Farther from where? Simplify it: the sensor flashes and listens at one spot on the wall.
lines.direction: VOICE: the forward question, answered in the same breath. PICTURE: the signature fold: room folds to the full-frame plan, characters become tokens, W1 glows; question title 'How does a delay become a location?'; confocal route out and back on W1; chip 'simplified picture · sends and listens at one spot'.

lines.text: Light covers about thirty centimetres every nanosecond. But the detour is there and back, so each extra nanosecond puts him only about fifteen centimetres farther from the wall spot.
lines.tts: Light covers about thirty centimetres every nanosecond. [lightly amused] But the detour is there… and back, so each extra nanosecond puts him only about fifteen centimetres farther from the wall spot.
lines.direction: VOICE: the round-trip turn is the small surprise; amused on 'there… and back'. PICTURE: the W1 to him leg as a ruler; a pulse runs out and back along it; the path meter fills two strokes per stroke of distance; labels '1 ns ≈ 30 cm of travel' 'there and back → ≈ 15 cm farther'.

lines.text: Measure the extra delay, and you know how far he is from that spot. Not which direction. Just how far.
lines.tts: Measure the extra delay, and you know how far he is from that spot. Not which direction… Just how far.
lines.direction: VOICE: precise (v1 take; tighten the pause after 'spot.' to 0.35 s). PICTURE: the one worked example, one step at a time: '≈ 8.9 ns later' → '≈ 2.65 m there and back' → '≈ 1.33 m each way' (illustrative, W1); the ruler wavers on 'Not which direction'.

lines.text: He could be anywhere on this arc, all the same distance from that spot.
lines.tts: He could be anywhere on this arc, all the same distance from that spot.
lines.direction: VOICE: J3 setup (v1 take; measures fast, listen). PICTURE: the arc sweeps from W1, dashed (a constraint, not a light path); J3a in the S4 face inset: he relaxes and leans on the partition; 'distance known · direction unknown'.

lines.text: Now listen at a second spot. Another delay, another arc. On this side of the wall, they cross in just one place.
lines.tts: Now listen at a second spot. Another delay, another arc. On this side of the wall, they cross in just… one place.
lines.direction: VOICE: J3 payoff (v1 take; tighten the pause after 'spot.' to 0.35 s). PICTURE: W4 lights, second arc, they cross at his token; the other crossing behind the wall greys out ('behind the wall: impossible'); J3b: his smile drops.

lines.text: Measured timings are a bit fuzzy, so each arc is really a band, and the bands overlap in a small patch.
lines.tts: Measured timings are a bit fuzzy, so each arc is really a band, and the bands overlap in a small patch.
lines.direction: VOICE: honest uncertainty (v1 take). PICTURE: arcs thicken into bands; the overlap fills as a patch; 'illustrative'.

lines.text: These two spots are close, so the patch is long and blurry. Spread them out, and it shrinks.
lines.tts: These two spots are close, so the patch is long and blurry. Spread them out, and it shrinks.
lines.direction: VOICE: rule of thumb (v1 take). PICTURE: spots slide together (W2, W3): long blurry patch; apart (W1, W4): it shrinks; 'close → long, blurry' then 'spread out → smaller'.

lines.text: In practice, a computer weighs many spots at once, trying positions and keeping those whose predicted echoes match. It also leans on assumptions, like what kind of object it's after.
lines.tts: In practice, a computer weighs many spots at once, trying positions and keeping those whose predicted echoes match. It also leans on assumptions, like what kind of object it's after.
lines.direction: VOICE: clear, unhurried (v1 take; tighten the pause after 'match.' to 0.35 s). PICTURE: four spots flash; candidate dots scatter; one candidate's predicted ticks laid against the measured ticks (miss fades, match stays); the rest cluster on him; 'assumption: one small object'.

lines.text: That's why the answer is a likely location, or a rough shape.
lines.tts: That's why the answer is a likely location, or a rough shape.
lines.direction: VOICE: settle. PICTURE: the cluster settles into a soft likely-location blob, never a dot; 'likely location'.

v1_fragment_alt.use: only if the listening pass prefers it to the new take and it splices cleanly; cut inside the measured silence

lines.text: And here's a real one.
lines.tts: [warmly] And here's a real one.
lines.direction: VOICE: discovery, warm, short. PICTURE: hard visible switch: new board, kraft palette, 'Real data', the same 3x3 zone icon as the waveform; 6 x 6 position grid still empty.

lines.text: Moved through known positions, the sensor behind that faint bump rebuilt the rough outline of a hidden U.
lines.tts: Moved through known positions, the sensor behind that faint bump rebuilt the rough outline of a hidden U.
lines.direction: VOICE: second evidence payoff (v1 take, moved from v1 5:06); hold on the finished U. PICTURE: the zone box steps through 36 preset positions; the U builds from the real partial sums (k = 1 to 36, no in-betweens); labels 'same 3x3 sensor · 36 preset positions · object held still' 'rough outline'; not morphed from our arcs.

lines.text: In 2012, an MIT team rebuilt the rough 3D shape of a hidden mannequin. By 2021, others had live video around corners.
lines.tts: In 2012, an MIT team rebuilt the rough 3D shape of a hidden mannequin. By 2021, others had live video around corners.
lines.direction: VOICE: brisk storyteller. PICTURE: the U board rolls up like a plan sheet and drops onto a museum shelf (chapter title 'How new is this?'); truck past the 2012 exhibit (table-sized rig, teal mannequin outline), the 2018 plate in passing, the 2021 exhibit (big laser, blobby live monitor); plates name year and team only; 'illustrations based on the papers'.

lines.text: But those ran on research equipment. One team had even tracked hidden objects with a cheap sensor.
lines.tts: But those ran on research equipment. One team had even tracked hidden objects with a cheap sensor.
lines.direction: VOICE: the precedent stated plainly, not as a twist. PICTURE: velvet rope clips across the exhibits under 'research equipment'; spotlight finds the stool with a fingertip-sized sensor board: '2021 · tracking with a cheap sensor kit (Callenberg et al.)'.

v1_fragment_alt.use: only if the listening pass prefers it to the new take and it splices cleanly; cut inside the measured silence

lines.text: Then, in a study published in 2026, a team from MIT and Dartmouth tried the small time-of-flight sensors, often called LiDAR, found in phones and gadgets.
lines.tts: Then, in a study published in 2026, a team from MIT and Dartmouth tried the small time-of-flight sensors, often called /ˈlaɪdɑːr/, found in phones and gadgets.
lines.direction: VOICE: the news beat (v1 take; LiDAR from IPA, listen). PICTURE: the checker's arm sets her sensor on the fourth plinth; spotlight isolates it; it matches to two drawn hardware types: 'smartphone-grade research device' and 'off-the-shelf kit'; plate 'published 2026 · MIT + Dartmouth'.

lines.text: Don't expect your phone to do this yet: phone makers often keep the raw data private.
lines.tts: Don't expect your phone to do this yet: phone makers often keep the raw data private.
lines.direction: VOICE: friendly caveat (v1 take; measures fast, listen). PICTURE: generic phone (no brand) slides in; a padlock closes over 'raw data'; small 'per the lead researcher, in interviews'.

lines.text: Their new idea: a model that keeps track of what moved, so many weak frames can be combined.
lines.tts: [warmly] Their new idea: a model that keeps track of what moved… so many weak frames can be combined.
lines.direction: VOICE: the answer to 'how new': warm, clear, attributed to them. PICTURE: back on the plinth: a stack of faint frames fans out beside the sensor; a small 'what moved' arrow ticks on each; label 'their new idea (2026)'.

lines.text: Why would a smaller, cheaper sensor need that?
lines.tts: [curious] Why would a smaller, cheaper sensor need that?
lines.direction: VOICE: a genuine question; 'that' points back to the new idea, and the next line answers it. PICTURE: spotlight close on the plinth sensor; question title 'Why is a cheap sensor harder?'.

lines.text: Weak lasers mean fainter echoes. The team's smartphone-grade device had about a hundred pixels: a hundred listening spots. And if you hold one in your hand, it jiggles.
lines.tts: Weak lasers mean fainter echoes. The team's smartphone-grade device had about a hundred pixels: a hundred listening spots. [lightly amused] And if you hold one in your hand, it jiggles.
lines.direction: VOICE: three problems as a quick rhythm; small smile on 'jiggles'. PICTURE: three full-frame beats, one at a time: dim beam and an even smaller echo on the hook's timeline; the research module's uncountable dot field, then its spots bunched on a small wall patch give the long blurry patch from C; the checker lifts the sensor off its stand and it jiggles.

v1_fragment_alt.use: only if the listening pass prefers it to the new take and it splices cleanly; cut inside the measured silence

lines.text: Their fix borrows night mode's trick from phone cameras: stack many quick, dim frames into one better estimate.
lines.tts: Their fix borrows night mode's trick from phone cameras: stack many quick, dim frames into one better estimate.
lines.direction: VOICE: clear (v1 take). PICTURE: six dim grainy plan frames slide into a stack and merge into one clearer card; 'our analogy: night mode'.

lines.text: The catch: things move between frames. He steps, and his echo shifts in time. The sensor jiggles, and its listening spots land somewhere new.
lines.tts: [dryly] The catch: things move between frames. He steps, and his echo shifts in time. The sensor jiggles… and its listening spots land somewhere new.
lines.direction: VOICE: the problem, plainly; two changes, two sentences. PICTURE: full-frame plan (chip 'illustration'); his token starts pacing with a grin (his plan: keep moving); first his step H_A to H_B and his echo tick slides on a mini timeline; then the sensor shifts and its spots slide along the wall.

lines.text: Just add them up, and echoes from different places blur into one smear, like a long exposure of someone walking.
lines.tts: Just add them up, and echoes from different places blur into one smear… [lightly amused] like a long exposure of someone walking.
lines.direction: VOICE: plain, then amused on the comparison. PICTURE: the two frames stacked as they are: a coral streak covering both positions ('just adding → smear', illustrative); 1 s gag: a streaky long-exposure snapshot of the guesser mid-walk; in the face inset he grins.

lines.text: So their model solves for one unknown at a time.
lines.tts: [warmly] So their model solves for one unknown at a time.
lines.direction: VOICE: the turn to the solution. PICTURE: three large icons 'shape' 'position' 'sensor'; padlocks close on two while the third stays free, two quick cycles; label 'one unknown at a time'.

lines.text: To build a shape, hold the object still and step the sensor through known positions, spreading out its listening spots. That's how the U was made.
lines.tts: To build a shape, hold the object still and step the sensor through known positions, spreading out its listening spots. That's how the U was made.
lines.direction: VOICE: explainer; callback lands on 'the U'. PICTURE: full-frame plan: still object, the sensor slides on a rail A to B1 (layout's two frames), new listening spots appear, the long patch shrinks modestly (about 30%, never to a dot); 1.5 s thumbnail of the real U board with its 'Real data' header; labels 'object still' 'sensor on a rail, at known positions'.

lines.text: To follow a person, hold the sensor still, and let each guess drift a little between frames, keeping the ones that still match. The estimate keeps up instead of smearing.
lines.tts: To follow a person, hold the sensor still, and let each guess drift a little between frames, keeping the ones that still match. [warmly] The estimate keeps up… instead of smearing.
lines.direction: VOICE: explainer, then the visible payoff, warm. PICTURE: sensor on its stand; his token walks H_A to H_D; each frame the candidate cloud drifts a little, poor guesses fade, the rest follow him; then two panels, one at a time: 'just adding → smear' and 'tracking what moved → keeps up'; he deflates in the inset; small label 'handheld: shown only for locating the sensor itself (reported)'.

lines.text: So what can it actually do, and where does it fail?
lines.tts: [curious] So what can it actually do… and where does it fail?
lines.direction: VOICE: curious; the last big question. PICTURE: the right-hand panel match-cuts to the real kit board (visible switch to 'Real data'); question title 'What can it do? Where does it fail?'; the stored estimate replays, sped up.

lines.text: Take our opening clip: an off-the-shelf kit the authors put at under a hundred dollars, held still while a person walked behind a partition.
lines.tts: Take our opening clip: an off-the-shelf kit the authors put at under a hundred dollars… held still while a person walked behind a partition.
lines.direction: VOICE: evidence voice, specific; callback to the opening; 'Take' is plain and brisk, not a question (lead's edit: 'that second case' lost its referent after the n24 question). PICTURE: the kit board gains the provenance the opening left out, one item at a time: 'ST sensor kit · 16 zones · held still · not the phone-grade device' 'under US$100 (authors' figure)' 'setup: flat wall + empty-room scan first'; frame counter 'frame N of 475'; small chip 'our check: their code + their data → matched their saved results · a software check, not a new experiment'.

lines.text: Many of their tests had help: safety-vest style reflective material on the target, which sends far more light straight back.
lines.tts: Many of their tests had help: safety-vest style reflective material on the target, which sends far more light straight back.
lines.direction: VOICE: conditions as useful understanding, not a disclaimer. PICTURE: plan close-up (not the room camera): a reflective strip on a target faces the wall and the incoming light; the returning pulse fattens; 'reflective material: far more light back'.

lines.text: Our clip's files don't say if the walker wore any.
lines.tts: Our clip's files don't say if the walker wore any.
lines.direction: VOICE: plain. PICTURE: back on the kit board: a small stamp beside the track, 'clothing: not recorded'.

v1_fragment_alt.use: only if the listening pass prefers it to the new take and it splices cleanly; cut inside the measured silence

lines.text: But in a separate test, the authors report tracking a person in ordinary clothes, capturing thirty frames a second.
lines.tts: But in a separate test, the authors report tracking a person in ordinary clothes, capturing thirty frames a second.
lines.direction: VOICE: fair and plain. PICTURE: framed card, plainly a drawing: neutral grey 'their sensor', a generic person in everyday clothes behind a partition; 'Reported by the authors · ordinary clothes · 30 frames/s capture' 'a separate test, not our kit clip · different device · data not released' 'our drawing'.

v1_fragment_alt.use: only if the listening pass prefers it to the new take and it splices cleanly; cut inside the measured silence

lines.text: What might this be good for? Picture a delivery robot nearing a blind warehouse corner.
lines.tts: [curious] What might this be good for? Picture a delivery robot nearing a blind warehouse corner.
lines.direction: VOICE: curious (v1 take). PICTURE: match cut: the card's partition becomes the warehouse's blind corner; 'potential use' top-left from the cut through n33; the robot rolls toward the corner, no long wait.

lines.text: With a suitable wall at the junction, a sensor like this might give it an early hint of movement out of sight.
lines.tts: With a suitable wall at the junction… a sensor like this might give it an early hint of movement out of sight.
lines.direction: VOICE: same words as v1 s41, new take: 'suitable' and 'might' need room (v1 takes were 272 wpm). PICTURE: plan of the junction: the wall spot lights; a pulse runs robot to wall spot to hidden aisle and back around the corner's end, never through shelving; a faint blob appears; no range number.

audio.note: text identical to v1 s41; new take because all four v1 takes are rushed (272 wpm articulated)

lines.text: Just a fuzzy blob: enough to say slow down, not enough to say who's there.
lines.tts: Just a fuzzy blob: enough to say slow down, not enough to say who's there.
lines.direction: VOICE: concrete benefit and its limit (v1 take). PICTURE: front view: the blob beyond the corner; the robot squints and brakes; 'slow down' 'not who'.

lines.text: And plenty is still hard: short range, dark or shiny walls, bright sunlight, and fast math on small hardware. The researchers call it an early-stage prototype.
lines.tts: And plenty is still hard: short range. Dark or shiny walls. Bright sunlight. And fast math on small hardware. The researchers call it an early-stage prototype.
lines.direction: VOICE: four short beats, then a plain attribution (v1 take; tighten the pause after 'hardware.' to 0.40 s). PICTURE: one full-frame tile per beat on the warehouse plan, then the four shrink into a row; 'early-stage prototype (the researchers)'.

lines.text: For now, it's a promising clue, not a safety system.
lines.tts: [softly] For now, it's a promising clue, not a safety system.
lines.direction: VOICE: settled, honest; the answer to the section's question. PICTURE: front view: the robot creeps on round the corner, slowly (the bumper gag is cut: J4 is the film's one closing gag); label 'not a safety system'; 'potential use' leaves with the cut.

v1_fragment_alt.use: only if the listening pass prefers it to the new take and it splices cleanly; cut inside the measured silence

lines.text: Being out of sight isn't the same as giving nothing away.
lines.tts: Being out of sight… isn't the same as giving nothing away.
lines.direction: VOICE: the takeaway, calm. PICTURE: hard cut from the warehouse corner to our room, the opening's raised view; one slowed round trip via W3 (no number) around the partition's end; the readout shows a soft blob; the guesser gulps.

v1_fragment_alt.use: only if the listening pass prefers it to the new take and it splices cleanly; cut inside the measured silence

lines.text: To really hide, he'd have to block the bounces too.
lines.tts: To really hide, he'd have to block the bounces too.
lines.direction: VOICE: J4 (v1 take); 3.0 s hold after it (v1 5.3 s). PICTURE: he pushes the partition back until it meets the wall; the paths stop at it; the readout goes blank; smug again; the checker simply leans round the near end and looks (J4); hard cut on the beat.

lines.text: This is Future Got Weird: the strange future, explained. Subscribe for more, and we'll see you around the corner.
lines.tts: [warmly] This is Future Got Weird: the strange future, explained. Subscribe for more, and we'll see you around the corner.
lines.direction: VOICE: one brief invitation (v1 take), from 0.2 s into the end screen. PICTURE: end screen: wordmark top-left, empty guides for one video element and the subscribe element, small callback art; see SHOTPLAN_V2 V13.

scenes.title: The kit clip and its conditions

proposed_claims_to_add_before_lock.P01: One unknown at a time: shape-building assumes known sensor positions and a still scene; tracking assumes a fixed sensor and a known (point) shape; locating the sensor assumes a known, still hidden object (reported by authors).
proposed_claims_to_add_before_lock.P02: Adding (filtered backprojection over) frames fails for moving objects because of motion blur (reported by authors).
proposed_claims_to_add_before_lock.P03: The tracking filter predicts, compares and keeps: about 1,000 guesses, a random step of 7 cm per frame in the released code, scored against each new frame and resampled (code_or_data).
proposed_claims_to_add_before_lock.P06: The ams bump at 3.70 ns is 110.8 cm of extra path, about 55 cm each way, consistent with the reconstructed U about 0.54 m from the wall (derivation).
proposed_claims_to_add_before_lock.P08: Replaces C38: on 8 October 2026 we re-ran the authors' released code (commit 15314de) on their released data; the tracking run matched their saved estimates (median 8 cm apart) and the U matched exactly; a software check, not a new experiment or a replication.

decisions: Hook question n06 stays inside the first 30 s, as the brief has it.
Software check stays on screen (kit-board chip) and in the description; not spoken.
